raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`HarmonyParser`, used by the `gpt-oss` tool-call detector and the gpt-oss reasoning parser, has three scans that go super-linear on model output:

1. Until a parsing strategy is chosen, the whole buffer is re-searched **on every chunk** with `(?:^|\s)(?:assistant)?\s*(analysis|commentary|...)`, which backtracks O(W²) over a whitespace run of length W. `TextStrategy.parse` runs the same search.
2. `TextStrategy`'s `^\s*(?:assistant)?\s*` prefix and `(.*?)\s*assistantfinal` backtrack the same way over whitespace.
3. `iter_tokens` slices `text[marker_pos:]` and re-runs `find("|>")` to the end of the text for every unknown `<|` marker.

| Input | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| one 16-char streaming chunk after `x` + 32,000 spaces | **23.7 s** | 3 ms |
| 32,000 leading spaces + `analysis` | 18.5 s | 10 ms |
| 80k unknown `<|a` markers | ~7x per doubling | linear |

Parsing runs synchronously on the tokenizer manager's event loop, so one such response stalls every in-flight request. Found with an Atheris fuzzing harness that records per-input parse time.

## Modifications

- The two strategy-detection searches only feed a true/false check. `(?<!\S)(?:assistant\s*)?(...)` accepts exactly the same strings (the keyword, or `assistant` followed by whitespace and then the keyword, must be preceded by whitespace or the string start) without the backtracking.
- `TextStrategy` patterns: `^\s*(?:assistant\s*)?(...)` matches the same prefixes as `^\s*(?:assistant)?\s*`. The `\s*` before `assistantfinal` is dropped: the lazy group still stops at the same (first) `assistantfinal`, and its only consumer calls `.strip()`, which removes exactly what `\s` would have.
- `iter_tokens`: the tail is sliced only when it is short enough to be a partial token (`<= len("<|constrain|>")`, the longest literal), and the last `|>` lookup is reused while it is still ahead of the current marker.
- Regression test `TestEdgeCases::test_long_whitespace_and_unknown_markers_parse_in_linear_time` (also asserts the parsed events): 105.7 s on `main`, 0.10 s here.

## Accuracy Tests

- Each rewritten regex vs the original on 500k strings: identical (31k – 237k matches per regex).
- `iter_tokens`: identical token streams on 300k strings.
- Differential test of `main` vs patched `GptOssDetector` and `HarmonyParser` under random re-chunking: **0 mismatches** over 80k inputs (49k events).
- `test/registered/unit/function_call/` + `test/registered/unit/parser/`: 1143 passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

See the table above.

Related: #42573 – #42583 (same issue class in other tool-call parsers).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (N/A)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@@ -43,6 +43,18 @@ def prefix_hold(text: str, tokens: List[str]) -> Tuple[str, str]:
     return text[:-max_hold], text[-max_hold:]
 
 
+_MAX_TOKEN_LEN = len("<|constrain|>")
+
+# Same truthiness as `(?:^|\s)(?:assistant)?\s*(...)`, which backtracks
+# quadratically over whitespace runs.
+_TEXT_FORMAT_CHANNEL_REGEX = re.compile(

+)

+    r"(?<!\S)(?:assistant\s*)?(analysis|commentary|assistantfinal)", re.IGNORECASE
+)
+
+
 def iter_tokens(text: str, start_pos: int = 0) -> Iterator[Token]:
     """Iterate over structural tokens in left-to-right order."""

@@ -57,6 +69,7 @@ def iter_tokens(text: str, start_pos: int = 0) -> Iterator[Token]:
 
     pos = start_pos
     has_unknown_tokens = False
+    next_close = None
     while pos < len(text):
         # Find next "<|"
         marker_pos = text.find("<|", pos)
@@ -77,8 +90,11 @@ def iter_tokens(text: str, start_pos: int = 0) -> Iterator[Token]:
                 found_token = True
                 break

-            tail = text[marker_pos:]
-            is_partial = any(lit.startswith(tail) for lit in TOKENS)
+            # A tail longer than every literal cannot be a partial token; skip
+            # the slice, which would copy the rest of the text per unknown marker.
+            is_partial = len(text) - marker_pos <= _MAX_TOKEN_LEN and any(

@@ -90,8 +106,11 @@ def iter_tokens(text: str, start_pos: int = 0) -> Iterator[Token]:

-                # Try to find a closing "|>" for this unknown token
-                close_pos = text.find("|>", marker_pos + 2)
+                # Try to find a closing "|>" for this unknown token, reusing the
+                # last lookup while it is ahead; a find per marker is quadratic.
+                if next_close is None or -1 < next_close < marker_pos + 2:
+                    next_close = text.find("|>", marker_pos + 2)

-                r"^\s*(?:assistant)?\s*(analysis|commentary)(.*)\s*$",

+import time
 import unittest
 
 from sglang.srt.parser.harmony_parser import (
@@ -628,6 +629,27 @@ def test_consecutive_blocks_same_type(self):

+    def test_long_whitespace_and_unknown_markers_parse_in_linear_time(self):
